subject: Post-demo follow-up: SDK auth + tool-calls + queue/autoscale sizing clarifications
messages:

Subject: Post-demo follow-up: SDK auth + tool-calls + queue/autoscale sizing clarifications

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and super helpful detail on your traffic patterns. This thread captures the follow-ups we promised from our side so your engineering and ops teams can validate before we scope Dedicated sizing formally. I grouped items into "integration" and "capacity" so it's easier to action.

Integration (SDK/Auth/Routing/Tool-calling)
- SDK bootstrap: we showed the Node + Python quickstart. Your engineering ask: can the SDK support service-account-based auth for Dedicated (no shared API key in app env)? Short answer: yes — we provide a service account token flow with short-lived JWTs and automatic rotation via your KMS. Karthik will add the auth diagram.
- Routing: you want routing by workspace_id -> dedicated pool, and fall back to hosted for batch jobs. We recommend a routing policy that pins low-latency calls to the Dedicated pool and tags batch jobs with "batch=true" to route to cheaper hosted instances.
- Structured outputs / tool calling: we can enable tool_call metadata so you can route invocations to internal microservices (e.g., invoice_calc). The SDK includes a tool-calling helper that produces structured JSON + action hints; see the diagram attached.
- Embeddings / reranker path: your plan to embed candidate sets in precompute then call a reranker at request time is supported. Note: we recommend keeping reranker model on Dedicated to avoid cross-environment latency.

Capacity (Dedicated sizing / autoscale / queues)
- Baseline numbers you gave: 250 TPS of short chat-style requests during peak (avg 40 tokens per request) and 30 r/s for reranker RPCs (reranker ~ 512 context).
- Initial suggestion (see attached sizing sheet): min_pool = 2 nodes, target_pool = 4 nodes, burst_pool = 6 nodes. Concurrency target per node: 40 concurrent streams for chat; reranker pinned at 8 concurrency per node when colocated.
- Queues: we propose a request-queue with backpressure threshold at 500 outstanding requests and graceful reject at 1000 requests to protect latency SLOs. Autoscale trigger: CPU or GPU util sustained > 70% for 30s or queue length > 250.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-sheet.xlsx (workbook with scenarios), auth-flow-diagram.png (service-account flow), reranker-cost-estimates.pdf (cost delta when reranker colocated).

Next steps (action owners):

- Tom/Rachel: confirm whether the reranker must be colocated in your VPC or can be hosted (reply with "colocate: yes/no").
- Mina: coordinate a short 30-min ops call w/ FinLogic infra + Redwood infra to validate queue/backpressure numbers (propose Tue 3/20).

Thanks — Mina

Appreciate the thorough recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Service-account auth: we can support a short-lived JWT model but need to be explicit about where keys live. Our security team requires that Redwood not have a copy of our private keys; can the rotation happen entirely on our KMS and only exchange public material with Redwood?

2) Reranker: for latency reasons we're leaning toward colocating the reranker in our VPC (colocate: yes). Question: if we colocate the reranker, do we still need a dedicated node for reranker-heavy traffic or can it share nodes used for chat with pinning?

3) Queues/backpressure: the proposed graceful reject at 1000 seems high for our user-facing endpoints. Can we model a per-endpoint soft limit at 200 and a hard per-system limit at 800?

We can do the ops call Tue 3/20 — Rachel and I are available 10:00-11:30 PT.

Tom — good questions, answered inline below. Forwarding the updated auth diagram and a lightweight runbook as attachments.

> rotation happen entirely on our KMS and only exchange public material with Redwood?
Yes. We support a mutual-TLS-style handshake where your KMS signs a short-lived CSR; Redwood uses the signed public cert to mint a dedicated-session token. No private keys are stored on Redwood. I'll attach the "auth-flow-diagram.png" and a step-by-step exchange for your security team.

> if we colocate the reranker, do we still need a dedicated node for reranker-heavy traffic or can it share nodes used for chat with pinning?
Short answer: you can share nodes and use scheduling/pinning. But a few caveats:
- Reranker uses large context (512) and tends to be CPU/GPU memory heavy; if reranker traffic spikes independently of chat, it can cause head-of-line interference.
- Option A (recommended): pin a small number of instances (1-2) with reranker runtime to absorb steady reranker load and let chat autoscale on remaining nodes. This avoids noisy neighbor effects.
- Option B: colocate fully and rely on priority queues + token-based preemption; this is lower-cost but operationally more complex.

> Can we model a per-endpoint soft limit at 200 and a hard per-system limit at 800?
Yes — Redwood supports per-route quota and a global queue cap. Implementation suggestion: per-route soft_limit=200 with exponential backoff response (429 + Retry-After) and global_hard_limit=800 returning 503s for excess traffic. We'll add these vars to the sizing sheet.

Attached: auth-flow-diagram.png (service-account exchange), redwood-dedicated-sizing-sheet.xlsx (updated row for per-route soft limits). Also include a short snippet for SDK config:

// set REDWOOD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN via local agent that talks to your KMS

client.generate({model: 'gptx-redwood-rl', input: '...'}).then(...)
